translations.text: The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.
To know wisdom and discipline, and to understand words of insight;
to receive discipline, reverence, righteousness, justice, and uprightness;
to give shrewdness to the simple, and knowledge and discretion to the young.
Let the wise listen and add to their wisdom, and let those with understanding acquire guidance,
so that they may understand proverbs and puzzling sayings, the words of the wise and their riddles.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, but the wicked despise knowledge and discipline.
My son, listen to your father’s teaching, and do not forget your mother’s teaching.
For they are an adornment for your head and a necklace for your neck.
My son, if sinners entice you, do not consent.
And if they say to you, “Come with us! Let us lie in wait to shed blood; let us hide to ambush the innocent without cause.
Let us swallow him alive like Sheol, and the blameless like those who go down to the pit.
We will find all his wealth and treasures, and fill our houses with plunder.
Cast your lot among us, and let us all have one purse.”
My son, do not go along the road with them, but keep your foot from their paths.
For their feet run toward evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood.
It is in vain that they spread traps for a bird.
They lie in wait to shed blood and conceal themselves.
Such are the ways of all who do wrong: they take the lives of those who follow them.
Wisdom is praised in the streets, and in the public squares she raises her voice.
At the head of the open spaces she proclaims, and at the entrances of the city gates she speaks her words:
How long, you childish people, will you love childishness? How long, you mockers, will you crave mockery, and you fools hate knowledge?
If you turn to my correction, I will pour out my spirit to you and make my words known to you.
Because I called and you did not believe, and I raised my voice and you did not listen,
and you despised all my counsel and wanted none of my correction,
I too will laugh at your ruin, and rejoice when turmoil and destruction suddenly come upon you,
and your ruin comes like a whirlwind, and when distress and anguish come upon them.
Then they will call me, but I will not answer them; they will come to me early, but they will not find me.”
Because they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the Lord,
and did not want my counsel, and rejected all my correction,
they will eat the fruit of their ways and be filled with their own schemes.
Therefore the waywardness of the simple will kill them, and the error of those who lack sense will destroy them.
But whoever listens to me will live in hope and be free from the many evils.
My son, if you accept my words and store up my commandments in your heart,
and incline your ear to wisdom and turn your heart toward understanding,
and call out for understanding and raise your voice for understanding,
and seek it like silver and search for it like treasure,
then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
For the Lord gives wisdom, and from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
He preserves hope for those who are upright and helps those who walk without blame.
He guards the paths of justice; he will guard the ways of his faithful ones.
Then you will understand righteousness and justice and the uprightness of all good paths.
When wisdom enters your heart and knowledge becomes pleasant to your soul,
good judgment will guard you, and the understanding of the righteous will rescue you.
So that you may be rescued from evil paths and from men who speak perverse things.
Those who abandon the straight path and walk in the way of darkness,
who rejoice in doing evil and delight in evil conduct—
their ways are crooked, and their paths are twisted.
Wisdom will deliver you from the foreign woman who twists her words,
who has abandoned the one who brought her up in her youth and forgotten the covenant of her God.
She has forgotten the thresholds of her house and the courses of her paths.
All who go in to her do not return, nor do they remember the path of life.
Therefore walk in the way of the good and keep to the path of the righteous.
For the upright will dwell in the land, and those who are blameless will remain in it.
Sinners will perish from the land, and the wicked will be uprooted from it.
My son, do not forget my law, and let your heart keep my commandments.
For length of days and years of life will be added to you.
Do not let peace, kindness, and truth leave you. Instead, tie them around your neck and write them on the tablets of your heart.
So that you may find mercy, favor, and understanding before God and before people.
Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not rely on your own wisdom.
Acknowledge him in all your ways, and he will make your paths straight.
Do not be wise in your own eyes, but fear the Lord and turn away from evil.
So that it may be healing for your flesh and nourishment for your bones.
Honor the Lord with your possessions and with the first of all your produce.
Then your storehouses will be filled with plenty, and your winepresses will overflow with wine.
My son, do not reject the Lord’s discipline, and do not grow weary of his correction.
For the Lord disciplines the one he loves, like a father who disciplines his son.
Blessed is the person who finds wisdom, and the mortal who finds understanding.
For the profit she brings is better than the profit from silver, and her yield is better than refined gold.
For she is more precious than precious stones, and nothing compares with her.
Length of days is in her right hand, and wealth and honor are in her left.
Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths are peace.
She is a tree of life to those who hold firmly to her, and blessed are those who wait for her.
The Lord laid the earth's foundations by his wisdom and established the heavens by his understanding.
And by his knowledge the depths were split open, and the clouds sprinkled dew.
My son, do not regard keeping my teaching and my counsel as something trivial.
And they will be life to your soul and refreshment to your neck.
Then you will walk confidently in your ways, and your foot will not stumble.
You will sleep without fear; you will lie down, and your sleep will be pleasant.
Do not be afraid of sudden turmoil or of the onslaught of sinners when it comes.
For the Lord will be with you and will keep your foot from being caught.
Do not hold back from doing good as long as it is in your power to do it.
When you have something to give, do not say to your neighbor, “Go away and come back tomorrow, and I will give it to you.”
Do not plot evil against your neighbor who lives peacefully with you.
Do not quarrel unjustly with anyone.
Do not envy a wicked man or desire any of his ways.
For the wicked person is unclean before the LORD, but the LORD shares his counsel with the upright.
The LORD’s curse is on the houses of the wicked, but he will bless the dwelling of the righteous.
He will overthrow mockers, but he will care tenderly for the wise.
The wise will inherit honor, but fools will receive disgrace.
Listen, children, to a father’s instruction, and pay attention to knowledge and understanding.
For I have given you good teaching; do not abandon my law.
For I was a son to my father, cherished and an only child in my mother’s eyes.
He taught me and said to me, “Let my word take firm hold in your heart. Keep my commandments and live, and guard my law like the pupil of your eye.”
Acquire wisdom and acquire understanding, and do not turn aside from the words of my mouth.
Do not abandon her, and she will protect you; love her, and she will rescue you.
The beginning of wisdom is this: acquire wisdom, and with all you acquire, acquire understanding.
Cherish her, and she will exalt you; embrace her, and she will honor you.
She will place the beauty of favor on your head and satisfy you with a crown of glory.
Listen, my son, and accept my words, and the years of your life will increase.
I have taught you the ways of wisdom and led you along straight paths.
When you walk, your steps will not falter, and if you run, you will not stumble.
Hold firmly to my instruction and do not abandon it. Guard it, because it is your life.
Do not walk in the path of sinners, and do not seek to follow the way of the wicked.
Do not pass through the place where they dwell, but turn aside and pass away from it.
For they do not sleep until they have done evil, and their sleep is disturbed until they have done what they want.
For their food is the food of wickedness, and they drink the wine of violence.
But the path of the righteous is like a shining light; its light keeps growing until the day is fully bright.
But the path of the wicked is darkness, and they do not know what makes them stumble.
My son, pay attention to my words and incline your ear to what I say.
Do not let them depart from your eyes, but keep them within your heart.
For they are life to whoever finds them and healing for his whole body.
Guard your heart with all vigilance, because from it comes the source of life.
Put crooked speech away from you, and keep [?] talk far from your lips.
Let your eyes look straight ahead, and let your eyelids be directed straight before you.
Turn your foot away from evil paths, and let all your ways be firmly established.
Do not turn aside to the right or to the left, but turn your foot away from evil.
My son, listen to my wisdom, and incline your ear to what I say,
so that you may exercise sound judgment and your lips may preserve knowledge.
For the lips of an adulterous woman drip honey, and her words are smoother than oil.
But their outcome is more bitter than wormwood, for she is sharper than a double-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death; her steps lead to Sheol.
She does not walk on the path of life, for her paths lead astray and are unknown.
Now, children, listen to me, and do not turn aside from what my mouth says.
Keep your way far from her, and do not approach the door of her house.
So that you do not give your strength to others and your years to those who show no mercy.
And strangers will consume your strength, and the fruit of your labor will enter the house of strangers.
In your old age your own soul will reproach you, when the flesh of your body has wasted away.
And you will say, “Why did I hate discipline, and why did my heart reject correction?”
I did not listen to the voice of my teachers, and I did not incline my ear to those who instructed me.
I was nearly caught in every kind of evil, in the assembly and the congregation.
Drink water from your own cistern, and running water from your own spring.
Let your waters overflow in your streets, and let them flow in your streets.
Let them be yours alone, and let no strangers share them with you.
Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of your youth.
A loving doe and a loving gazelle: learn her ways at all times, and delight in her love.
Do not go astray, my son, with an adulterous woman, and do not embrace the bosom of an adulterous woman.
For a person's ways are before the eyes of the Lord, and all his paths lie open before him.
The wicked man will be caught by his own sins and bound with the cord of his own offenses.
He will die without discipline, and through his great folly he will go astray.
My son, if you have stood as guarantor for your neighbor and pledged your hand to a stranger,
you have been ensnared by the words of your mouth and caught by the speech of your lips.
Do this, my son, and escape: because of your friend you have fallen into your enemy's hands. So urge the friend for whom you have given a guarantee.
Do not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids,
so that you may escape like a gazelle from a snare and like a bird from a trap.
Imitate the ant, observe its ways, and learn: it has no harvester,
no ruler over it, and no one to compel it,
yet it prepares its bread in summer and gathers its food at harvest.
How long will you sleep, you lazy person? When will you rise from your sleep?
A little slumber, a little sleep, a little placing your hand on your chest.
Poverty will come upon you, and need will overtake you like a vigorous man.
A foolish person, a wicked man, goes about oppressing others.
He winks with his eyes, signals with his foot, and gestures with his fingers.
He is perverse in his heart, constantly devises evil, and stirs up strife between people.
Because of this, his ruin will come suddenly; suddenly he will be broken, and there will be no healing for him.
There are six things the Lord hates, and seven that he detests:
a haughty eye, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood;
a heart that devises [?] plans, and a foot that hastens to run toward evil;
a false witness who speaks lies, and one who stirs up strife among brothers.
My son, keep your father's commandment, and do not forget your mother's instruction.
Fix them in your heart continually, and bind them around your neck.
When you walk, keep them close to you, and let them be with you. Guard them so that they may guard you, and when you wake, let them be your meditation.
For the commandment is a lamp, and instruction is a light, and reproof and discipline are the way of life,
to keep you from an evil woman and from the slander of a foreign woman's tongue.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart. Do not be caught by her eyes, and do not let her capture you with her eyelashes.
For a prostitute is like a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts a precious life.
Can a person put fire in his lap without burning his clothes?
Or can a man walk on burning coals without scorching his feet?
So it is with someone who sleeps with his neighbor’s wife: whoever touches her will not go unpunished.
It is no surprise when someone is caught stealing, for he steals to satisfy his hunger.
But if he is caught stealing, he must repay sevenfold and give up everything he owns in his house.
But a man who commits adultery with a woman lacks sense and destroys himself.
He brings disgrace upon himself, and they will trample him down; his shame will not be forgotten.
For a husband’s anger is full of jealousy, and he will show no mercy on the day of revenge.
He will show no favor for a gift and will not be appeased, however large a bribe you offer him.
My son, keep my words and store up my commandments in your heart.
Keep my commandments and live; guard my teaching like the pupil of your eye.
Tie them around your neck and write them on the tablets of your heart.
Say to wisdom, “You are my sister,” and call understanding your close friend,
so that they may keep you from the foreign woman whose words are seductive.
For I looked out from the window of her house, through the lattice,
and saw the naive, and looked at young men who lacked sense,
passing through the street beside the corners of the paths to her house,
in the evening, at sunset, in the darkness of night and in the gloom.
A woman came out to meet him, dressed like a prostitute, who leads young men’s hearts astray.
She is rebellious and dissolute, and her feet never stay at home.
Instead, she wanders outside at one time and through the streets at another, and lies in wait at the corners.
She seized him and kissed him, and with a brazen face said to him,
“The sacrifices are peace offerings; today I have fulfilled my vows.
That is why I came out to meet you: I was longing to see you, and I have found you.
I have spread coverings on my bed and covered it with Egyptian fabrics.
I have sprinkled my bed with myrrh, saffron, and cinnamon.
Come, let us enjoy love until morning and embrace one another with desire.
For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey.
He took a bag of money with him, and he will return home after many days.
She led him astray with her many words and drew him to herself with her seductive lips.
He was following her like a child, like an ox going to slaughter, and like a dog going to be bound.
Like a deer into whose liver an arrow flies, he rushes like a bird into a trap, not knowing that he is going to his own death.
Now, children, listen to me and pay attention to the words of my mouth.
Do not let your heart turn toward her ways, and do not wander into her paths.
For she has struck down many victims, and all those she has killed were mighty.
The paths to her house are paths to Sheol, descending to the chambers of death.
Therefore proclaim wisdom, and understanding will answer you.
For wisdom is on the tops of the heights; she stands at the crossroads and beside the paths.
At the gates she calls out with her mouth, and at the entrances to the city gates she is praised.
She says, “To you, men, I call, and my voice is directed to humankind,
so that the simple may understand prudence, and those who lack sense may gain understanding in their hearts.
Listen to me, for I speak what is true, and when I open my mouth, I speak what is right.
For my mouth speaks truth, and lying lips are unclean in my sight.
All the words of my mouth are righteous; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.
They are all clear to anyone who understands them, and straightforward to anyone who wants to know them.
Accept instruction rather than silver, and choose knowledge for yourselves rather than refined gold.
For wisdom is better than refined gold and better than precious stones, and nothing compares with her.
I, wisdom, created prudence, and I possess knowledge and discretion.
The fear of the Lord hates evil. I hate pride, arrogance, the evil way, and a perverse mouth.
Counsel and instruction are mine; understanding is mine, and strength is mine.
Through me kings reign, and rulers decree justice.
Through me rulers exercise authority, as do nobles and all who judge justly.
I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
Riches and honor are mine, along with enduring wealth and righteousness.
My fruits are better than refined gold, and my produce than choice silver.
I walk in the way of righteousness, along the paths of justice,
to give those who love me hope as their inheritance and to fill their treasuries.
The Lord created me at the beginning of his creation, before all his works.
He established me before the ages, from the beginning, before the earth was established.
I was born before the depths existed, before there was water in the springs.
Before the mountains were established, before the hills, I was conceived,
before he made the earth and the valleys and the first dust of the world.
When he established the heavens, I was with him, and when he made a circle over the surface of the depths,
when he strengthened the clouds above and strengthened the springs of the depths,
when he set a law for the sea so that the waters would not overstep his command, and when he made the foundations of the earth,
I was beside him, setting things in order. He delighted in me every day, and I was always rejoicing before him.
I rejoiced in his inhabited earth and took pride in human beings.
Now, children, listen to me. Blessed is the one who keeps my ways.
Listen to instruction and become wise; do not go astray.
Blessed is the person who listens to me, keeping watch at my gates every day and guarding the thresholds of my doors.
For my ways are ways to life, and favor comes from the Lord.
Those who sin against me harm themselves, and all who hate me love death.
Wisdom built a house and set up seven pillars in it.
She slaughtered her animals, mixed her wine, and prepared her tables.
She sent her servants to call out on the heights and say:
“Whoever is inexperienced, let him come to me.” And to whoever lacks understanding, say:
“Come, eat my bread and drink the wine I have mixed.
Put away your lack of understanding and live; choose the straight path.”
Whoever disciplines an evil person brings disgrace on himself, and whoever rebukes a wicked person brings a stain on himself.
Do not rebuke an evil person, lest he hate you; instead, rebuke a wise person, and he will love you.
Give advice to a wise person, and he will become still wiser; instruct a righteous person, and he will increase his learning.
The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and knowledge of the righteous is understanding.
For through her your days will increase, and years of life will be added to you.

My son, if you are wise, you are wise for yourself and for your friends. But if you become evil, you alone will bear your evil deeds. Whoever makes a false denial tends the winds and chases the birds of the sky. For he has left the path of his vineyard and strayed from the paths of his work to walk in a waterless wilderness. Leaving the well-trodden way, he wanders in thirst; he too will gather nothing.
A woman who lacks sense is seductive and knows no shame.
She sits at the door of her house, on a high seat.
She calls to those passing along the road, whose paths are straight, and says:
“Whoever is naive, let him come to me.” And to the one who lacks sense he says:
“Stolen water is sweet, and hidden bread is pleasant.”

He does not know that mighty men perish with her, and that all her guests are in the depths of Sheol. But hurry away and do not linger in that place. Do not let your eye be caught there. For in this way you will pass foreign waters and cross a foreign river. Turn away from foreign waters, and do not drink foreign waters, so that many days and years of life may be added to you.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a son who lacks understanding brings shame to his mother.
There is no benefit in the treasures of wickedness, but righteousness delivers from death.
For the Lord does not let the righteous person go hungry, but he overthrows the possessions of the wicked.
Poverty humbles a person, but diligent hands bring wealth.
Whoever works in summer is a sensible son, but whoever sleeps during harvest is a son who brings shame.
A blessing will rest on the head of the righteous, but wickedness will cover the mouth of the wicked.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will die out.
One whose heart is wise will accept a command, but one whose lips are contemptuous will be caught.
Whoever walks with integrity will walk confidently, but whoever follows crooked paths will be found out.
Whoever winks deceitfully causes pain, but whoever rebukes openly makes peace.
The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but wickedness will cover the mouths of the wicked.
Hatred stirs up conflict, and shame will cover all the wicked.
Whoever brings wisdom from his lips strikes the senseless person with a rod.
The wise store up knowledge, but a hasty mouth is close to ruin.
The possessions of the rich are strong fortresses, but the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
The work of the righteous leads to life, but the income of the wicked leads to sin.
The path of life preserves discipline, but whoever hates correction goes astray.
The lips of the wicked conceal hostility, and whoever utters a curse lacks sense.
With many words, wrongdoing cannot be avoided, but whoever restrains his lips is sensible.
The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked is gall.
The lips of the righteous are very merciful, but fools will die for lack of understanding.
The blessing of the Lord makes rich, and no sorrow will accompany it.
A fool does evil while laughing, but wisdom is a man's understanding.
The wicked person is driven toward destruction, but hope is given to the righteous.
As a whirlwind suddenly passes, so the wicked person will perish and no longer be found. But the foundations of the righteous will be established forever.
Just as sour grapes hurt the teeth and smoke hurts the eyes, so the wicked person hurts those who employ him.
The fear of the Lord adds days, but the years of the wicked will be shortened.
The hope of the righteous brings joy, but the hope of the wicked will perish.
The way of the Lord strengthens the blameless but brings ruin to those who do wrong.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not dwell in the land.
The mouth of the righteous speaks wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut off.
The lips of the righteous know kindness, but the mouths of the wicked speak perverse things.
The Lord rejects dishonest scales and is pleased with accurate weights.
Where insolence enters, disgrace enters, but wisdom belongs to the humble.
The hope of the upright will be built up, but the arrogance of the wicked will be overthrown.
Wealth is no help on the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death.
The righteousness of the blameless person will make his path straight, but the wicked person falls through his wickedness.
The righteousness of the upright will deliver them, but the wicked will be caught in their wickedness.
When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of evil people perishes.
The righteous person will be delivered from distress, and the wicked person will enter it in his place.
The wicked person destroys his neighbor with his mouth, but the righteous will be strengthened through knowledge.
Through the prosperity of the righteous, a city grows strong, and at the destruction of the wicked it rejoices.
Through the blessings of the upright, a city is exalted, but through the mouths of the wicked it is overthrown.
Whoever despises his neighbor lacks understanding, but a discerning man remains silent.
A slanderer reveals secrets, but someone faithful in spirit keeps a matter hidden.
A people without a leader falls, but its deliverance comes through many counselors.
The wicked man does harm whenever he meets the righteous, because he hates those who wait in hope.
A compassionate woman brings honor to a man, but a woman who hates truth is a throne of disgrace. Lazy people become needy even with their wealth, but strong people uphold knowledge.
A godly man lays up good [?] for himself, but a man without compassion destroys his own body.
The wicked man labors in sweat, but the reward of the one who sows righteousness is certain.
A son of righteousness is destined for life, but the one who does evil is destined for death.
The Lord rejects those whose hearts are crooked, but he delights in those whose way is blameless.
Whoever stretches out his hand against his neighbor will not escape evil, but the descendants of the righteous will be delivered.
Like a gold ring in a sow’s snout is a beautiful woman without good judgment.
The desire of the righteous is for good things, but the hope of the unjust ends in wrath.
One person sows what belongs to him and brings in much; another gathers what does not belong to him, yet has little.
A blessed person will prosper, but a cursed person will be cursed again.
The one who withholds grain in a time of distress will be abandoned to his enemies, but a blessing will rest on the head of the one who sells it.
Whoever seeks good seeks favor, but evil will come upon the one who seeks it.
Whoever trusts in his wealth will fall, but the righteous will flourish like leaves.
Whoever builds his household on terror will leave his children sighs. Whoever does not work in his household will distribute winds to his children, and a fool will become a servant to the wise.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, but the lives of the unjust are scattered.
If the righteous person barely survives, where will the wicked person and the sinner be found?
Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, but whoever hates correction is a fool.
It will go well for the man who observes the Lord’s will, but an unjust man will be condemned.
No one will be established through his injustice, but the root of the righteous will not be shaken.
A capable woman is her husband's crown, but like a beetle and a worm in wood, a woman who does evil destroys a man.
The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the conduct of the unjust is deceitful.
The words of the unjust lie in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright delivers them.
The wicked will be overthrown and will be found no more, but the house of the righteous will stand firm.
People praise an intelligent mouth, but one who lacks understanding will be despised.
Better is a poor man who serves himself than someone who boasts but lacks bread.
A righteous person understands the needs of his animal, but the wicked withhold their compassion.
Whoever works the land will have enough bread, but whoever pursues worthless things lacks understanding.
The wicked person longs to do evil, but the root of the righteous will sprout.
An evil person is trapped by the wrongdoing of his lips, but a righteous person escapes distress.
A good man will be satisfied by the fruit of his mouth, and everyone is repaid according to the work of their hands.
A fool's way looks good in his own eyes, but whoever listens to advice is wise.
A fool makes his anger known immediately, but a shrewd person conceals an insult.
A righteous person speaks evident truth, but an unjust witness is deceitful.
Some people's words are a striking sword, but the tongue of the wise heals.
Truthful lips are upright, but a hasty witness has a dishonest tongue.
Deceit is in the heart of the evil person who devises evil, but those who counsel peace will have joy.
Nothing [?] is fitting for a righteous man, but the wicked are full of evil.
The Lord rejects lying lips, but he delights in those who act faithfully.
A shrewd person is a throne of knowledge, but the heart of fools calls out for evil.
The hand of the diligent will rule, but the deceitful will be subjected to tribute.
A frightening word disturbs a person's heart, but a good word makes it glad.
A righteous person gives good advice to his friend, but the way of the wicked leads them astray.
A deceitful man will not obtain his prey, but an excellent person is a precious possession.
In the path of righteousness there is life, but the path of the resentful leads to death.
A wise son listens to his father, but an evil son who does not accept correction will perish.
A good man will be satisfied by the fruit of his mouth, but the lives of the wicked will perish.
Whoever guards his mouth safeguards his life, but whoever opens his lips brings ruin on himself.
A person who does no work is always caught up in cravings, but the appetite of the diligent will be richly satisfied.
The righteous person hates false speech, but the wicked person will be ashamed and disgraced.
Righteousness guards the person whose way is blameless, but the sinner’s sin will destroy him.
Some make themselves out to be rich but have nothing, while another makes himself out to be poor but possesses great wealth.
A person’s wealth is the ransom for his life, but the poor person does not receive a rebuke.
The light of the righteous will rejoice, but the lamp of the wicked will go out.
An evil person acts wickedly and disgracefully, but those who take advice are wise.
Wealth gained through injustice will diminish, but wealth gathered through righteousness will increase.
A person who begins to help is better than one who keeps hope hanging, and hope that comes to fulfillment is a tree of life.

Whoever despises the word will be ruined by it, but whoever fears the commandment will be saved. A deceitful man will receive no favor, but a wise man whose deeds are upright will also rise to the top in his course.
The teaching of wisdom is a fountain of life for those who turn away from the snares of death.
Good understanding wins affection, but the way of the wicked leads to destruction.
Everything a prudent person does is done with knowledge, but a fool speaks empty words.
A wicked messenger falls into trouble, but a faithful messenger is a healer.
Poverty and disgrace put an end to discipline, but whoever heeds correction will be honored.
A beautiful desire delights the soul, but the impurity of the wicked is separated from knowledge.
Whoever walks with the wise will become wise, but whoever walks with fools will suffer harm.
Trouble pursues sinners, but the righteous will be rewarded with good things.

A good man leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren, and the sinner's wealth is stored up for the righteous. Those whose lives did not last many years lost their wealth, and some perished completely.
Whoever spares his rod hates his son, but whoever loves his son disciplines him diligently.
The righteous person eats and is satisfied, but the stomachs of the wicked will lack food.
A wise woman builds her house, but a foolish woman tears it down with her own hands.
Whoever walks uprightly fears the Lord, but whoever is crooked in his ways despises him.
In a fool’s mouth are a sting and disgrace, but the lips of the wise protect them.
Where there are no oxen, the feeding troughs are clean, but abundant crops come through an ox’s strength.
A faithful witness does not lie, but someone who speaks falsehood is a lying witness.
An evil person seeks wisdom but will not find it, while knowledge is readily available to the discerning.
Everything is against a foolish man, but the lips of the wise are a weapon of knowledge.
A prudent person understands his way through his wisdom, but the way of fools leads astray.
The households of the wicked rightly need purification, but the households of the righteous are accepted. Fools commit sins, but the children of the upright enjoy favor.
A discerning heart has sorrow of its own, and no stranger will share in its joy.
The house of the wicked will perish, but the tent of the upright will rejoice.
There is a way that people think is right, but its paths are paths of death.
Even in laughter the heart may ache, and the end of its joy is sorrow.
Someone whose heart is insolent will be satisfied by his own ways, and a good man will be satisfied by his own reverence.
A naive person believes every word, but a prudent person distinguishes good from evil.
A wise person is cautious and turns away from evil, but a fool confidently becomes involved in it.
A rash person acts without taking advice, but a wise man is gentle.
Fools inherit folly, but prudent people distribute knowledge.
The wicked will fall before the good, and evildoers will come to the gate of the righteous.
A poor person is hated even by his friends, but a rich person has many friends.
Whoever despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is the person who has compassion on the poor.

The wicked go astray by doing evil, but the compassionate and righteous do every kind of good. Those who do evil will not understand mercy and faithfulness, but compassion and faithfulness are with those who do good.

In everything you work at, there is something to be gained. Whoever is modest in his way of life will be gentle and pleasant. The Lord heals every pain, but the speech of the wicked impoverishes them.
The crown of the wise is their wealth, and the conduct of fools is their folly.
A truthful witness saves lives, but a false witness speaks deceit.
In the fear of the Lord there is strong confidence, and he will be a refuge for his children.
The fear of the Lord is a fountain of life for those who turn away from the snares of death.
A king is honored by a large population, but when the people come to an end, the king is ruined.
A patient person is very wise, but an impatient person is very foolish.
Someone who cools his anger is a healer of his own soul, but envy rots the bones.
Whoever treats a poor person very badly angers his Maker, but whoever honors the Lord has compassion on the poor.
The wicked person is overthrown by his wickedness, but whoever is confident that he has no sins is righteous.
Wisdom will dwell in the heart of the upright, but in the heart of fools it will not be known.
Righteousness exalts a people, but sins bring nations low.
A king favors an understanding servant, but the wicked person is overthrown by his own wisdom. Whoever is confident that he has no sins is righteous, but anger destroys even the wise.
A gentle word turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
The tongue of the wise makes knowledge attractive, but the mouth of fools spews curses.
The eyes of the Lord are everywhere, watching the good and the wicked.
A healing tongue is a tree of life, and whoever eats its fruit will be satisfied by it.
A fool mocks his father's discipline, but a prudent person pays attention to correction.
There is great wealth in the house of the righteous, but the earnings of the wicked will perish.
The lips of the wise speak knowledge, but the hearts of fools are not upright.
The Lord rejects the sacrifices of the wicked, but he delights in the prayer of the upright.
The Lord rejects the way of the wicked, but he loves whoever practices righteousness.
The discipline of those who do not know evil is evident, and those who hate correction will die.
Sheol and destruction lie before the Lord, and so do human hearts.
An evil person does not love someone who corrects him, and he does not walk with the wise.
A joyful heart makes the body look well, but an aching heart causes the spirit pain.
The heart of the righteous seeks knowledge, but the mouth of the wicked speaks evil things.
All the days of the poor are bad, but the cheerful are always at ease.
For one who fears the Lord, a little is better than the great treasures of the wicked.
A meal of vegetables with love of the name [?] is better than fattened oxen with hatred.
A hot-tempered man stirs up conflict, but a patient man puts it out before it begins.
The paths of the lazy are full of thorns, but the paths of the upright are smooth.
A wise son makes his father glad, but a foolish son is his mother's shame.
A foolish man lacks sense, but a discerning man walks uprightly.
Those who delay [?] the assembly frustrate plans, but through many advisers a plan is established.
A man finds joy in the words of his mouth, and it is good for him to speak at the right time.
For the discerning, the path of life leads upward, so that they may turn away from Sheol below.
The Lord uproots the house of the proud, but he secures the boundaries of widows.
Evil thoughts are detestable before the Lord, but pleasant words are pure.
Whoever accepts a bribe destroys himself, but whoever hates taking bribes will live.
The heart of the righteous meditates on faithfulness, but the mouth of the wicked speaks evil things.
The Lord is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
The light of the eyes gladdens the heart, and a cheerful heart nourishes the bones.
The ear that listens to life-giving correction will dwell among the wise.
Whoever rejects discipline hates himself, but whoever listens to correction gains wisdom.
The fear of the Lord is instruction for life, and the praise of the humble person goes before him.
The plans of the heart come from a person, but the speech of the tongue comes from the Lord.
All a man's ways are pure in his own eyes, but the Lord sets his path straight.
Make your deeds known to the Lord, and your plans will be established.
All the Lord's works are for those who obey him, and the wicked person is kept for the day of trouble.
Everyone who is proud in heart is unclean before the Lord, and someone who stretches out his hand against his neighbor will not be cleared of wrongdoing.
Through kindness and truth, wrongdoing is forgiven, and the fear of the Lord turns people away from evil.
When a man's ways please the Lord, he will repay even his enemies.
A little with righteousness is better than abundant income without justice.
A person's heart plans his ways, but the Lord directs his steps.
An oracle is on the king's lips, and his mouth does not err in judgment.
The weight of the scales is the Lord's judgment, and all his works are true weights.
Kings who do wrong are defiled, for a throne is established through righteousness.
The king delights in the lips of the righteous person, and he loves the speech of the upright.
The king's anger is a messenger of death, but a wise man will quench it.
In the light of the king's face there is life, and his favor is like a cloud of early rain.
For whoever acquires wisdom, it is better than gold, and for whoever acquires understanding, it is more valuable than silver.
The path of the upright turns away from evil, and whoever takes care of himself guards his way.
Disgrace comes before ruin, and a proud spirit before sickness.
Someone humble in spirit and modest in his gaze is better than someone who divides plunder with the mighty.
Whoever understands a matter finds good, and blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord.
Someone wise in heart knows understanding, and someone whose lips are reverent increases learning.
Understanding is a fountain of life to those who know it, but the instruction of fools is contemptible.
A wise heart knows what its mouth should say and adds learning to its lips.
The speech of a wise person is a honeycomb; it is sweetness to his soul and healing to his bones.
There is a way that seems right in people's eyes, but its paths are paths of death.
A suffering soul has its own pains, and destruction comes to it from its own mouth.
An unjust man forges evil, and fire burns from his mouth.
An unjust man stirs up conflict, and a worthless man drives away his friends.
An unjust man entices his companion and leads him along a way that is not good.
He winks his eyes and plots perverse things; he signals with his lips and carries out evil.
Old age is a crown of glory, and it is honored on the path of righteousness.
A patient person is better than a mighty warrior, and one who controls himself is better than one who captures a city.
The lot falls into the lap of contention, and its verdict comes from the Lord.
Dry bread in peace is good, better than a house full of sacrificial feasts accompanied by conflict.
A sensible servant will rule over a son who brings shame, and will share the inheritance among the brothers.
The crucible tests silver, and the furnace gold, but the Lord tests the heart.
An evil man listens to wicked lips, but a righteous man does not listen to a wicked tongue.
Whoever mocks the poor angers their Maker, and whoever rejoices at disaster will not go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and parents are the glory of their children.
Trustworthy speech does not suit a fool, nor does lying speech suit a righteous person.
A stone of favor is beautiful in its owner's eyes, and wherever it turns, it brings understanding.
Whoever covers an offense seeks friendship, but whoever refuses to cover it separates himself from friend and neighbor.
A rebuke crushes the heart of a wise person, but a fool is beaten instead of being rebuked and does not notice.
A quarrelsome man seeks evil, and a merciless angel is sent against him.
Anxiety and fear fall upon a wise man, and upon a fool in his foolishness.
Whoever repays good with evil will never have evil depart from his house.
Whoever sheds blood stirs up a lawsuit before the ruler.
Whoever acquits the guilty and condemns the righteous is unclean before the Lord.
Why does wealth go to a fool who has no heart to acquire wisdom?
A friend is loving at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
A foolish person gives his hand in pledge, standing as guarantor for his neighbor.
Whoever loves wrongdoing loves trouble and strife, and whoever raises his gate high seeks his own ruin.
Someone with a crooked heart finds no good, and someone with a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.
Whoever fathers a fool brings shame on himself, and the fool's father will not rejoice in him.
A joyful heart does the body good, but a wounded spirit dries up the bones.
Whoever takes a bribe is wicked, for he perverts the course of justice.
The discerning person's face is turned toward wisdom, but the fool's eyes are on the depths of the earth.
A foolish son angers his father and brings bitterness to the woman who bore him.
It is not good to humiliate the righteous, nor to beat righteous people who speak what is right.
Whoever restrains his words has knowledge, and whoever is patient is a wise man.
A fool who keeps silent is considered wise, and someone whose lips are still is considered discerning.
And in his silence he dwells on desire and mocks good instruction.
A fool has no desire for wisdom, because his heart dwells on foolishness.
When a wicked person reaches the depths of evil, foolishness, dishonor, and reproach come upon him.
The words of a person's mouth are deep waters, and the fountain of wisdom is a flowing stream.
It is not good to show favoritism to the wicked, nor to pervert justice against the righteous.
A fool's lips enter into disputes, and his mouth brings him to death.
A fool's mouth is his own ruin, and with his lips he traps himself.
The words of a lazy person throw him into trouble, and they bring him down to the chambers of Sheol.
Whoever lets his hands grow slack at his work is a brother to a destructive man.
The name of the Lord is a strong tower; the righteous run to it and are secure.
Honor and wealth are his fortified city, and his dwelling is within a strong wall.
Before ruin, a person's heart becomes proud, and before honor comes humility.
Whoever gives an answer before listening is a fool and is put to shame.
A person's spirit bears his suffering, but who can bear a wounded spirit?
An upright heart acquires wisdom, and a wise ear listens to knowledge.
A person's gifts make room for him and bring him before great people.
A person is in the right in his own case, but when his neighbor comes, he examines him.
Casting lots settles disputes and decides between the powerful.
A brother helped by his brother is like a city because of its strength, and its locks are like the bar of a fortress.
A man's stomach will be filled with the fruit of his mouth, and he will be satisfied with the produce of his lips.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and whoever loves it will eat its fruit.
Whoever finds a good wife finds something good and receives favor from the Lord. Whoever sends away a good wife sends goodness out of his house.
The poor person speaks gently, but the rich person speaks harshly.
There are friends who are friends, and there is a friend who stays closer than a brother.
A poor person who walks in integrity is better than a rich person whose ways are crooked.
It is not good for someone not to know himself, and whoever is hasty on his feet sins.
A man's foolishness makes his ways crooked, yet in his heart he complains against the Lord.
Wealth adds many friends, but a poor person is separated from his friends.
A false witness will not be acquitted, and whoever speaks lies will not escape.
Many serve before a great man, and he gives gifts to those who are wicked.
All the poor man's brothers hate him, and even his friends keep far away from him. Anyone who is [?] in his words is not trustworthy.
Whoever acquires wisdom loves himself; whoever preserves faithfulness finds good.
A false witness will not be acquitted, and whoever speaks lies will perish.
Luxury is not fitting for a fool, nor is it fitting for a slave to rule over princes.
A man's understanding is his patience, and his glory is to overlook a wrong.
The king's anger roars like a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
A foolish son is a disgrace to his father, and a wife's complaining is like a dripping leak.
A house and wealth are an inheritance from a father, but it is from the Lord that a wife is betrothed to a man.
Drowsiness brings sleep, and a lazy person will go hungry.
Whoever keeps the commandment safeguards his life, but whoever is careless about his ways will be killed.
Whoever lends to the Lord has compassion on the poor, and he is repaid according to his deeds.
Discipline your son, because there is hope, but do not set your heart on humiliating him.
An angry man receives punishment, and the more he rises, the more he adds to his burden.
Listen to advice and accept discipline, so that you may become wise in your ways.
There are many plans in a person's heart, but the Lord's purpose will stand.
What is desired in a person is kindness, and a poor person is better than a rich man who lies.
The fear of the Lord leads to life. Whoever is satisfied with it will rest and will not encounter evil.
The lazy man who hides his hands in his lap will not even bring them to his mouth.
When a fool is beaten, the wise take warning; and if you correct a wise person, he gains understanding.
A son who despises his father and distresses his mother brings shame and disgrace.
Stay, my son, and listen to discipline, and do not stray from the words of knowledge.
An unjust witness makes judgment oppressive, and the mouth of the wicked drowns him.
Pains are prepared for those who make judgment oppressive, and blows for a foolish people.
Wine is strong, and drunkenness is insulting; whoever indulges in it is not wise.
A king's anger roars like a lion, and whoever provokes him sins against his own life.
It is to a man's credit when he ends a quarrel, but every fool mocks.
The lazy man is reproached but does not keep silent; he asks at harvesttime, but there is no water.
A word lies deep in a king's heart, but a wise man will draw it out.
Many people are called merciful, but who can find a faithful man?
A righteous man walks in integrity; blessed are his children after him.
A king sits on the throne of judgment, and all evils are scattered before him.
Who can say, “You are pure, my heart, and I have been cleansed of sins”?
Differing weights and differing measures are both detestable before the Lord.
Even a child is known by his deeds, whether he is pure and whether his actions are upright.
The ear that hears and the eye that sees—the Lord made them.
Do not love sleep, or you will become poor. Instead, open your eyes and have your fill of bread.
A friend will say to his companion, “I have bought it,” and then boast.
And let us say that there is gold, an abundance of precious stones, valuable vessels, and lips of knowledge.
Take the cloak of someone who guarantees a stranger's debt, and take his pledge on behalf of strangers.
Bread gained through deceit tastes sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth will be filled with gravel.
A plan is established through counsel, and war is waged through strategy.
A slanderer reveals secrets, but someone trustworthy in spirit conceals a matter. Do not associate with someone whose lips are hasty.
Whoever curses his father or mother—his lamp will go out like the dark pupil of an eye.
An inheritance acquired hastily at the beginning will not be blessed in the end.
Do not say, “I will repay evil.” Instead, wait for the Lord to rescue you.
Differing weights are unclean before the Lord, and dishonest scales are not good.
A person's steps come from the Lord. Who, then, can set his own course?
It is a trap for someone to vow something as holy and then, after making the vow, regret it.
A wise king scatters the wicked and rolls a wheel over them.
The human breath is the Lord's lamp, searching all the innermost chambers of the body.
Kindness and truth protect the king, and his throne is established through kindness.
The glory of warriors is their strength, and the splendor of the elderly is their gray hair.
Crushing and torment strike the wicked, and blows reach the innermost chambers of their bodies.
Like a stream of water, the king's heart is in God's hands; he directs it wherever he wishes.
All a person's ways are right in his own eyes, but the Lord sets the heart right.
The Lord prefers someone who practices righteousness and justice to sacrifice.
Haughty eyes, a proud heart, and the lamp of the wicked are sin.
The plans of the chosen person are trustworthy, but those of the wicked bring loss.
Acquiring treasure with a lying tongue—and those who seek death will be swept away to destruction.
Destruction will come upon the wicked because they refused to practice justice.
A man whose way is crooked is a stranger, but the deeds of someone pure are upright.
It is better to sit on the corner of a roof than to live with a quarrelsome woman.
The soul of the wicked person is not seen in the eyes of his companions.
And through the wicked person's [?], the simple person becomes wise, and the wise person gains knowledge through reflection.
The righteous person understands the hearts of the wicked and drives the wicked toward disaster.
Whoever closes his ears so as not to hear the poor will himself call to God, and he will not answer him.
A gift given in secret turns away anger, but someone who begrudges giving stirs up anger.
The joy of the righteous brings about justice and crushes evildoers.
A person who strays from the path of understanding will rest with the children of the earth.
A man who is in need and loves pleasure, wine, and perfume will not become rich.
The wicked person is a substitute for the righteous, and the deceitful person for the upright.
It is better to live in a wilderness than to dwell with a quarrelsome and irritating wife.
Desirable treasure and oil are in the dwelling [?]; wisdom and human understanding will swallow it up.
Whoever seeks righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and praise.
A wise person climbs into the city of warriors and conquers the fortress in which it trusts.
Whoever guards his mouth and tongue guards himself from trouble.
The insolent man, whose name is “Mighty,” acts wickedly in his malice.
The lazy person's craving kills him, because he is unwilling to let his hands do any work.
All day long he craves more, but the righteous person gives without holding back.
The sacrifice of the wicked is unclean, because they bring it with wickedness.
A false witness will perish, but a person who listens speaks truthfully.
A wicked man's face is shameless, but an upright person sets his own paths straight.
There is no wisdom, understanding, or counsel like the LORD's.
The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but deliverance belongs to the LORD.
A name is worth more than great wealth, and compassion is better than gold and silver.
The rich and the poor meet one another, and the LORD made them both.
The prudent person sees a wicked man being flogged and is sternly instructed, but fools pass him by and suffer loss.
Humility is followed by fear of the LORD, wealth, honor, and life.
Snares and traps are on the difficult path; whoever guards himself will stay far from them.
Whoever disciplines a child according to his way—even when he grows old, he will not turn away from it.
The rich person will rule over the poor person, and a servant will lend to the one who used to lend to him.
Whoever sows injustice will reap trouble, and the rod of his anger will come to an end.
The generous person will be blessed, because he gives some of his bread to the poor.
Get rid of the wicked person and drive out the quarrelsome one, and disputes and insults will cease. Otherwise, if he sits in the assembly, he will insult you all.
God loves the one who is pure in heart, and shows mercy to the lips of the king’s friends.
The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge and destroy lying words.
When the lazy person is sent out, he says, “There is a lion on the road, and look, a murderer in the streets!”
The mouth of a foreign woman is a deep pit, and anyone with whom the Lord is angry will fall into it.
Foolishness distracts a child’s heart, but the rod of discipline drives it away from him.
Someone who oppresses the poor increases his own trouble, and someone who gives to the rich brings loss upon himself.
Incline your ear and listen to the words of the wise, and apply your heart to my knowledge.
Because they are pleasant, keep them within you, and let them all be ready together on your lips.
So that your trust may be in the Lord, I have made this known to you today.
Look, I have written them for you three times,
to make known to you counsel, knowledge, tranquility, and words of truth, so that you may return a truthful answer to the one who sent you.
Do not defraud the poor person because he is poor, and do not humiliate the afflicted at the gate.
For the Lord will plead their case and avenge the wrong done to their lives.
Do not be a friend to an angry man, and do not associate with a man full of rage,
lest you learn his ways and find a snare for yourself.
Do not pledge yourself as a guarantor because you feel embarrassed in front of people.
For if you have no means to repay, they will take your bedding from under you.
Do not move the ancient boundary marker that your ancestors set up.
If you see a man skilled in his work, he will stand before kings; he will not stand before obscure people.
If you sit down to dine with a ruler, pay attention to what is set before you,
so that you do not put a knife in your mouth if there is a man with a great appetite.
Do not crave his food, because his bread is the bread of deceit.
Do not approach a rich man, but use wisdom to get away from him.
For if you fix your eyes on it, you will no longer see it, because it makes wings for itself like an eagle and flies to heaven.
Do not dine with a stingy man, and do not crave his food.
For eating and drinking with him is like swallowing pitch, and his heart is not with you.
You will vomit up the bread you eat and waste your pleasant words.
Do not speak in front of a fool, because he despises your words.
Do not move an ancient boundary marker, and do not enter the field of orphans.
For their redeemer is strong, and he will plead their case against you.
Apply your heart to discipline and your ear to words of knowledge.
Do not withhold discipline from a child, for if you strike him, he will not die.
For you strike him with a rod and rescue his life from Sheol.
My son, if your heart is wise, my own heart will also rejoice.
My innermost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but live in the fear of the Lord all day.
Then you will have a future, and your hope will not come to an end.
Listen, my son, and be wise, and let my mind rejoice in your heart.
Do not get drunk on wine, and do not gorge yourself on meat.
For whoever gets drunk on wine and gorges on meat will perish, and whoever sleeps will wear sackcloth.
Listen to your father who brought you into the world, and do not despise your mother's old age.
Acquire truth, and do not sell wisdom, discipline, or understanding.
Let the father of a righteous person rejoice and exult; let him father a wise child, and let his father rejoice in him.
Let your father and mother rejoice in you, and let the woman who bore you exult.
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes watch my ways.
For a prostitute is a deep pit, and an adulterous woman is a well of distress.
She destroys without warning, and many people multiply wrongdoing.
Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has disputes? Who has troubles? Who has wounds for no reason? Whose eyes are discolored?
Who but those who linger over wine and search out places where there is a drinking house? Do not become drunk with wine, but speak with righteous people, and walk and talk with them.
Do not fix your eyes on wine whose color gleams in the cup, but meditate on righteousness.
For wine's end is like a snake's bite and like a flying viper.
When your eyes look at an adulterous woman, then your heart speaks perverse things.
You will be like someone lying down in the heart of the sea, like a sailor in a great storm.
You will say, “They struck me, but I felt no pain. They were mocking me, but I did not know it. When will I wake up and go looking for it?”
Do not envy evil people or desire to be with them.
For their hearts devise evil, and their lips speak injustice.
Through wisdom a house is built, and through understanding it is made secure.
Through knowledge its rooms are filled with every kind of wealth, honor, and delight.
A wise person is better than a strong one, and a knowledgeable person than a mighty warrior.
War is waged through strategy, and victory comes through many advisers.
Wisdom is too high for a fool, and he does not open his mouth at the gate.
Anyone who plans to do harm is called an evildoer.
A fool’s thinking is sin, and evil is what defiles a person.
Evil will lead the wicked away on the day of distress.
Rescue those who are being led to death, and do not hold back from redeeming those who are seized for slaughter.
If you say, “I do not know,” know that God searches the thoughts of the heart. The one who watches over your life knows, and he repays each person according to their deeds.
My son, eat honey, for it is good, and honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
In the same way, you will find wisdom for your soul, and you will have a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
Do not lie in wait, you evildoer, at the home of the righteous, and do not plunder his dwelling place.
For a righteous person falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked will be overthrown by calamity.
When your enemy falls, do not rejoice; when he is overthrown, do not let your heart exult.
Otherwise the Lord may see it and be displeased, and turn his anger away from him.
Do not be envious of evil people or jealous of evildoers.
For evil people will have no future, and the lamp of evildoers will be extinguished.
My son, fear the Lord and [?], and do not associate with fools.
For their ruin comes suddenly, and who knows the end of their years?
I say these things to the wise: Showing partiality in judgment is not good.
Nor is it good to say to an evildoer, “You are righteous.” Peoples will curse him, and nations will revile him.
The poor will find delight, and a good blessing will come upon them.
They will kiss the lips of those who rebuke.
Prepare your work outside and make things ready in your field; afterward, build your house.
Do not be a false witness against your neighbor, and do not deceive him with your lips.
Do not say, “I will do to him as he did to me, and repay him according to his deeds.”
I passed by the field of a lazy man and by the vineyard of a man lacking sense.
It grew up and was entirely filled with woodland; moles covered its surface, and its stone walls had collapsed.
I saw it, took it to heart, and learned a lesson.
And if you doze a little, sleep a little, and lay your hand on your chest a little—
Poverty will go before you, and need will overtake you like an armed man.
These too are the profound proverbs of Solomon, which the friends of Hezekiah, king of Judah, wrote down.
It is God's glory to conceal a matter, and a king's glory to investigate a matter.
The heavens are high, the earth is deep, and a king's heart cannot be searched out.
Remove the impurities from silver so that a pure vessel may come out.
Let the wicked be crushed before the king, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
Do not boast before a king, and do not stand in the place of the great.
For it is better that he say to you, “Come up higher,” than that he humiliate you before a ruler. Say what your eyes have seen.
Do not rush into a lawsuit, lest, when you pursue it, your friend disgrace you in the end.
Argue your case with your neighbor, but do not reveal another person's secret.
Otherwise, someone who hears may disgrace you, and many will grumble about you.
Someone who speaks a word is like a gold apple in silver filigree.
Like a gold earring and a fine carnelian, so is the rebuke of the wise to an ear that listens.
Just as snow falling on a harvest day cools the heat, so a faithful messenger refreshes those who send him and revives his masters' spirits.
Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of gifts that are a lie.
Through patience a ruler is persuaded, and a gentle tongue breaks bones.
When you find honey, eat only enough for yourself, lest you become overfull and vomit it up.
Do not go too often to your friend's house, lest he grow tired of you and hate you.
Like a club, a sword, and a sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbor.
Like a bad tooth and an unsteady foot is trust in a liar in a time of trouble.

Someone who takes a garment from his neighbor on a cold day is like someone who pours vinegar on a string and aggravates an aching heart. As a moth eats away at a garment and a worm at wood, so sorrow eats away at a person's heart.
If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink.
When you do these things for him, you heap burning coals on his head, and the Lord will repay you.
Like the north wind that brings forth rain are angry looks and a slanderous tongue.
It is better to live on a corner of the roof than to live with a quarrelsome wife in a house full of conflict.
Like cold water to a thirsty soul is good news that comes from a distant land.
Like someone who blocks a spring and ruins a watercourse is a righteous person who falls before the wicked.
Eating much honey is not good, nor is searching out words of praise.
Like a breached city without a wall is a man who has no patience.
Like snow in summer and rain at harvest, honor is not fitting for a fool.
Like a bird and a winged creature flying through the air, a groundless curse wanders away.
A whip for a horse and a goad for a donkey—so also a goad for a foolish man.
Do not answer a fool according to his foolishness, or you too will become like him.
Instead, speak to a fool according to your wisdom, so that he does not think himself wise.
Whoever sends a message through a fool drinks injustice from beneath his own foot.
If you give a lame man the ability to walk, you will receive a word from a fool's mouth.
Like a stone in a sling is someone who praises a fool.
Thorns sprout in a drunkard's hand, and foolishness in a fool's mouth.
A fool's body suffers greatly, and a drunkard crosses the sea.
Like a dog that returns to its vomit is a fool who acts foolishly in his folly.
If you see a man who is wise in his own eyes, a fool is far more sensible than he is.
When a lazy man is sent somewhere, he says, “There is a lion on the road, and a lion in the streets!”
Like a door that turns on its hinge, a lazy man turns over in his bed.
The lazy person who hides his hands in his lap finds it tiring to bring them to his mouth.
A lazy man is wiser in his own eyes than seven people who can give a reason.
Whoever meddles in a dispute that is not his own is like someone who grabs a dog by its ears.
Just as boastful people hurl words like sharp, deadly arrows,
so is a man who deceives his neighbor and, when they discover him, says, “I was joking!”
When there is no wood, the fire goes out; where there is no troublemaker, quarreling becomes quiet.
Charcoal for embers and wood for fire—and a quarrelsome man stirs up strife.
The words of a gossip cause turmoil and go down into the chambers of the heart.
Like worthless silver coating a clay pot are burning lips and an evil heart.
A hateful person is known by his lips, and treachery lies hidden within him.
Even if he softens his voice, do not trust him, because there are seven evils within him.
The evil of someone who conceals hatred in his heart will be exposed in the assembly.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone will have it roll back on him.
A lying tongue hates truth, and a gossiping mouth causes turmoil.
Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what it will bring forth.
Let a stranger praise you, not your own mouth; someone else, not your own lips.
A stone is heavy and sand is weighty, but a fool’s anger is heavier than both.
Wrath is ruthless and anger is violent, but who can stand before jealousy?
Open rebuke is better than hidden love.
A friend’s wounds are better than an enemy’s kisses.
A person who is full tramples on honeycombs, but to a hungry person even bitter things taste sweet.
Like a bird that leaves its nest is a man who wanders from his place.
Like oil and perfume that gladden the heart is someone who pleases his friend with heartfelt advice.
Do not abandon your friend or your father's friend, and do not enter your brother's house on the day of your disaster. A neighbor nearby is better than a brother far away.
Be wise, my son, and gladden my heart; remove from me the reproach of those who insult me.
A prudent person sees danger and hides, but the naive go on and suffer loss.
The cloak of someone who guarantees a stranger’s debt is taken; take a pledge from him on behalf of a stranger.
Someone who blesses his friend flatteringly in a loud voice is no different from someone who curses him.
Like a leak that drips on a rainy day is a quarrelsome wife.
The north wind is harsh, and it is called by the name of the south wind.
Iron sharpens iron, and a man sharpens his friend’s face.
Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever attends to his master will be praised.
Just as faces are not alike, so hearts are not alike.
Sheol and destruction are never satisfied; neither are human eyes satisfied.
A refiner tests silver, and a furnace tests gold; a man is tested by the mouths of those who praise him. The heart of the wicked seeks evil, but the heart of the righteous seeks knowledge.
Even if you beat a fool in the assembly, you do him no good, nor do you remove his foolishness.
When you tend your sheep, know their condition, and pay attention to your herd.
For possessions do not last forever, nor do they endure from generation to generation.
The hay flourished, the new grass appeared, and the grass of the mountains was gathered.
Lambs provide your clothing, and young goats your food.
And goats’ milk provides food for you and your household.
The wicked flee when no one pursues them, but the righteous are confident like a lion.
Because of a land’s wickedness, its rulers are many, but righteous people who understand justice will endure.
A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that brings no benefit.
Those who abandon the law boast of wickedness, but those who keep the law strengthen themselves.
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the Lord know all good things.
A poor person walks in integrity, while a rich person’s ways are crooked.
Whoever keeps the law is an understanding son, but whoever pursues worthless things brings shame on his father.
Whoever increases his possessions through interest and usury will leave them to someone who has compassion on the poor.
Whoever closes his ears to avoid hearing the law—even his prayer is unclean.
Whoever leads an upright person astray onto an evil path will fall into a pit, but the blameless will inherit good things.
A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but a poor man with understanding despises him.
When the righteous grow strong, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, it diminishes.
A person who conceals his wrongdoing will not prosper, but God will have mercy on someone who confesses his sins and turns away from them.
Blessed is the person who is always fearful, but whoever hardens his heart will fall into trouble.
A roaring lion and a growling bear—such is a wicked person who rules over a poor people.
A ruler who lacks understanding commits many acts of oppression, but whoever hates deceit will live long.
A person burdened with the blood of a life will flee to the grave, and no one will help him.
Whoever walks blamelessly will be saved, but whoever follows crooked paths will fall into a pit.
Whoever works the land will have plenty of bread, but whoever pursues worthless things will have plenty of poverty.
A faithful man has many blessings, but an evil man will not go unpunished for his wrongdoing.
A man who shows favoritism is not good, for he will betray someone for a piece of bread.
A stingy man hurries to become rich and does not know that deprivation is coming upon him.
Whoever rebukes someone finds more affection than someone who flatters with his tongue.
Whoever robs his father and mother and says, “I have committed no sin,” is a partner of a wicked man.
A greedy man stirs up conflict, but whoever trusts in the Lord will prosper.
Whoever trusts in his own heart is a fool, but whoever walks with integrity will escape.
Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing, but whoever turns his eyes away from the poor will receive many curses.
When the wicked rise, people hide, but when they perish, the righteous will increase.
A man who refuses correction and stiffens his neck will suddenly be broken, and there will be no healing for him.
When the righteous increase, the people increase, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
A man who loves wisdom will make his father glad, but whoever indulges in prostitution will lose his possessions.
A king establishes the land through justice, but a wicked man impoverishes it.
A man who quarrels with his neighbor spreads a net across his path.
An evil man is caught in his own wrongdoing, but the righteous will sing praises and rejoice.
For the righteous person knows the legal rights of the poor, but the wicked person has no understanding of such knowledge.
Mockers set cities on fire, but the wise turn away anger.
When a wise man argues with a fool, the fool rages and laughs and will not be appeased.
Bloodthirsty men hate the innocent person, but the righteous love him.
A fool pours out all his anger, but a wise person considers matters in his mind.
A ruler who listens to lies has servants who are all wicked.
The poor person and the oppressor meet one another, and the Lord gives light to the eyes of both.
A king who judges truthfully will have his throne established through justice.
The rod and correction give wisdom, but an undisciplined child brings shame to his mother.
When the wicked increase, wrongdoing increases, but the righteous will rejoice at their downfall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest and bring delight to your soul.
When the wicked multiply, the people are broken, but blessed is the one who keeps the law.
A slave is not disciplined by words, for he knows that he will not be beaten.
If you see a man who is hasty in his words, know that a fool is better than he is.
Whoever is pampered from his youth will become a servant, and in the end he will groan.
A hot-tempered man stirs up disputes, and an angry man multiplies wrongdoing.
A person's pride will bring him low, but his humility will increase his honor.
Whoever shares with a thief hates his own life. Oaths are imposed on him, but he does not confess.
A man's wrongdoing becomes a stumbling block for him, but whoever trusts in the Lord will be strong.
Many seek a ruler's favor, but a man's justice comes from the Lord.
An unjust man is abhorrent to the righteous, and an upright way is abhorrent to the unjust.
The words of Agur son of Jakeh, who received prophecy and gained strength, and spoke to Ithiel.
For my mind is deficient, and I lack human understanding.
I have not known wisdom, nor have I learned the knowledge of the holy ones.

Tell me: Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has held the wind in his hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in a cloth? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son's name, if you know?
All God's sayings are choice, and he helps those who trust in him.
Do not add to his words, lest he rebuke you and you be shown to be a liar.
I have asked two things of you; do not withhold them from me before I die.
Keep falsehood and lying speech far from me. Give me neither poverty nor wealth; give me enough to live on.
Otherwise I might become full and deny him, saying, “Who is the Lord?” Or I might become poor and steal and swear by the name of my God.
Do not hand a slave over to his masters, lest he curse you and you be found guilty.
A generation that insults its fathers and does not bless its mother.
A generation that is clean in its own eyes but has not been washed of its filth.
A generation—how haughty its eyes are, how lifted its eyelids!
There is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose fangs are knives, to devour the poor of the earth and the wretched among humankind.
The leech has three beloved daughters. There are three things that are never satisfied, and a fourth that never says, “Enough!”
Sheol, a woman whose womb is closed, the earth that is never satisfied with water, and fire that never says, “Enough!”
The eye that mocks its father and despises its mother's old age—the ravens of the valley will peck it out, and young eagles will eat it.
There are three things hidden from me, and four that I do not know:
The way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea, and the way of a man in his youth.
This is the way of an adulterous woman: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, “I have done nothing.”
Under three things the earth trembles, and under four it cannot endure:
under a slave when he becomes king, and under a fool who has eaten his fill of bread;
under a hated woman when she gets a husband, and under a maidservant who drives out her mistress.
There are four things that are small on the earth, yet they are wiser than the wise:
ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food in summer;
rock hyraxes, which have little strength, yet make their homes among the rocks;
locusts, which have no king, yet all gather together as one;
and the lizard, which takes hold with its hands and lives in kings’ houses.
There are three whose steps are stately, and four that walk well.
The young lion is stronger than every other animal; it is not afraid and does not turn back before any animal.
A rooster strutting among the hens, a male goat walking at the head of the flock, and a king speaking among the nations.
Do not covet, lest you be disgraced, and do not put your hand to your mouth in alarm.
From the fat of milk comes butter, and if you press your hand against the nose, blood comes out. So angry contention produces a lawsuit.
The words of King Lemuel, the prophet, whom his mother instructed, saying to him:
“Oh, my son! Oh, son of my womb! Oh, son of my vows!
Do not give your strength to women, or your ways to women who devour kings.
Beware of kings, Lemuel—of kings who drink wine and rulers who drink strong drink—
so that you do not drink and forget [?], and forget the rights of all the poor.
Strong drink is given to mourners, and wine to those whose souls are bitter,
so that they may drink and forget their pains, and remember their troubles no more.
Open your mouth with a truthful word, and judge all those who do wrong.”
Open your mouth with a just judgment, and judge the cases of the poor and the unfortunate.
Who can find a capable woman? She is more precious than priceless gemstones.
Her husband’s heart trusts in her, and she lacks no provisions.
She did him good and not harm all the days of his life.
She sought wool and flax, and the work of her hands was as she wished.
She was like a merchant’s ship, whose merchandise comes from far away.
She rose in the night and gave food to her household and work to her maidservants.
She considered a cultivated field and bought it, and with the fruit of her hands she planted a vineyard.
She girded her waist with strength and made her arms strong.
She tasted the success of her trade, and her lamp did not go out all night.
She stretched out her arms diligently and her hands to the spindle.
She opened her hands to the poor and stretched out her arms to the needy.
The members of her household were not afraid of snow, because they were all dressed in scarlet clothing.
She made herself a bed covering and garments of fine linen and purple.
Her husband was known among the cities when he sat among the elders of the land.
She made linen and sold it, and supplied belts to the Canaanites.
Strength and splendor are her clothing, and she will rejoice on the last day.
She opened her mouth with wisdom, and the teaching of compassion was on her tongue.
The ways of her household are clear to her; she did not eat her bread in idleness.
Her children rose and called her blessed, and her husband praised her.
Many of her daughters have acquired wealth, but you have surpassed them all.
Charm is deceptive and beauty is empty, but a woman who fears the Lord will be praised.
Give her some of the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her at the gate.
